questions.q: You want to compare total_spend across three sales channels. Which approach fits a numeric-versus-category pair?
options: A scatter plot of channel against channel
A crosstab of total_spend against itself
A single histogram of channel
groupby('channel') summaries (mean and median) or a box plot per channel
questions.explain: Numeric versus category is handled by summarizing the numeric column within each group, and box plots show each group's distribution.

questions.q: In the illustrative data, mean total_spend by channel was app 232.7, store 154.8, web 193.4, while the medians were about 128, 129, and 117. What is the best interpretation?
options: App customers clearly spend twice as much as store customers
The medians are wrong because they are lower than the means
The gap in means is largely driven by two extreme values, so the channels look similar in typical spend
Web is the least valuable channel because its median is lowest
questions.explain: Two very large values inflate the means of the groups they belong to. The medians, which resist outliers, show typical spend is similar across channels.

questions.q: Why normalize a crosstab with normalize='index' when comparing churn across regions?
options: It converts counts within each region to rates, so regions of different sizes are comparable
It sorts the regions alphabetically
It removes missing values
It adds a p-value to each cell
questions.explain: Raw counts depend on how many customers each region has. Row-normalizing gives the share who churned within each region.

questions.q: The correlation between tenure_months and orders was about 0.55. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Longer tenure causes more orders
Tenure and orders have a moderate positive association in this data
Tenure and orders are unrelated
Orders determine tenure exactly
questions.explain: A correlation of 0.55 is a moderate positive relationship. Correlation alone doesn't establish causation or exactness.

questions.q: South's churn rate (about 29%) is higher than East's (about 15%), but South has only 99 customers. What is the most responsible way to record this?
options: South is definitely the worst region and needs a retention program now
Ignore it because the group is small
A lead worth testing further, since a group this small can swing by chance
Delete the South rows to even out the sample
questions.explain: Group size limits how much you can trust a rate. Note it as a lead and test it (later lessons cover hypothesis tests) rather than declaring it settled.
